bio: Oyster Oyster, a Michelin-starred restaurant in Washington, D.C.'s Shaw neighborhood, has earned acclaim for its inventive cuisine and steadfast commitment to sustainability. Opened in 2020 by Chef Rob Rubba, who received the James Beard Award for Outstanding Chef in 2023, the restaurant is built on the idea that dining can be both extraordinary and environmentally responsible. Its ever-changing tasting menu is primarily plant-based, with the occasional inclusion of responsibly harvested oysters and other sustainable seafood, celebrating the Mid-Atlantic's bounty through close partnerships with local farmers and foragers. Every aspect of Oyster Oyster reflects ecological responsibility, from eliminating single-use plastics and using compostable materials to a beverage program focused on natural and biodynamic wines, while even the design incorporates reclaimed and repurposed elements to reduce waste. Each dish honors the natural world by showcasing vegetables, grains, and fungi with creativity and precision, offering a meal that is at once refined, thoughtful, and deeply connected to the environment, positioning Oyster Oyster as a model for the future of sustainable fine dining.
